panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Panel A is a human H&E section showing conventional gland-forming esophageal adenocarcinoma, matching the captioned diagnosis. B: Panel B shows human esophageal adenocarcinoma with poorly formed glands and focal discohesive growth, a non-tubular histologic pattern of the target disease. C: Panel C is human esophageal adenocarcinoma tissue with solid/nested growth and inflammation, supporting the target disease. D: Panel D shows discohesive human esophageal adenocarcinoma cells infiltrating desmoplastic stroma, a variant morphology of the target disease. E: Panel E is a human H&E section of poorly differentiated solid esophageal adenocarcinoma with inflammation, supporting the target disease. F: Panel F shows human esophageal adenocarcinoma with mucinous differentiation and neoplastic glandular clusters, a variant morphology of the target disease.
panels.attribution_text: Montalbano et al. SMARCA2 and SMARCA4-deficiency is associated with a distinct molecular and microenvironmental subtype of esophageal adenocarcinoma.. Scientific reports 2026. doi:10.1038/s41598-026-60346-8. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Representative H&E morphology of SMARCA-deficient esophageal adenocarcinoma, scale bars 50 μm (A) Conventional gland-forming adenocarcinoma with tubular/papillary architecture; (B) tumor with poorly formed glandular structures and focal discohesive growth; (C) Focal solid/nested growth pattern with accompanying inflammatory infiltrates; (D) discohesive tumor cell infiltration within a desmoplastic stromal background; (E) Poorly differentiated solid tumor component with prominent inflammatory background; (F) tumor with mucinous differentiation showing prominent extracellular mucin pools with floating neoplastic glandular clusters. Overall, SMARCA-deficient EACs showed a broad histomorphological spectrum encompassing both tubular and non-tubular patterns. Besides conventional gland-forming morphology, a subset of tumors displayed poorly formed glands, solid/nested growth, discohesive infiltration, prominent desmoplastic stroma, and variable inflammatory infiltrates. In some cases, intraluminal necrotic debris compatible with “dirty necrosis” was present. However, no recurrent morphology-specific pattern allowing reliable distinction from SMARCA-intact esophageal adenocarcinoma was identified.
in_text_mentions: conventional gland-forming tumors to cases with focal or more extensive non-tubular components. Although solid or discohesive growth, dirty necrosis, prominent desmoplasia, inflammatory infiltrates, and occasional mucinous differentiation were observed, we did not identify a recurrent or diagnostically distinctive H&E pattern that reliably separates SMARCA-deficient EAC from SMARCA-intact conventional EAC. These findings support the interpretation that SMARCA deficiency defines a molecular and microenvironmental subset of EAC rather than a strictly morphology-defined histological one (Fig. 3).
